authority: inclusion-criteria.json and the user's own-technology requirement
finding: The current final-held-primary-review.json overgeneralises commissioned development. Partner development of an organisation's own substantive platform can qualify; generic client-only implementation or staffing does not qualify solely because original code was written.
mainReview: Main independently read the UMB VBZ prototype case, icentic SME development/staffing offering and mecas physical-AI description. The first two prove client engineering but do not alone establish maintained technology of their own. Withdraw the main provisional keep endorsement for UMB and icentic; retain uncertainty pending specific own-technology evidence. Do not remove either record merely for uncertainty.
mecas: The company's stated physical-AI research/system development remains potentially qualifying, particularly under the generous young-startup rule; do not claim a released proprietary product from the homepage alone.
publication: No organisation or location was changed by this correction. CrowdSports remains qualifying because the commissioned platform is its own operational product.
requiredReconciliation: Final population totals must not treat the two provisional keep recommendations as settled evidence. Preserve the earlier reviews as evidence history, not as authoritative eligibility decisions.
